title: Ability to highlight icons across multiple displays in desktop Folder Views
line: Dragging a selection rectangle on the desktop now continues onto the other screens and selects their icons too.
explanation: Every screen's desktop is a separate Folder View with its own model and window, so a rubber band only ever existed in the view where the drag started and was clamped to that screen's edge. The other screens never learned about it, so their icons couldn't be reached by dragging (only by Ctrl+click). The view that owns the drag now shares the band in global coordinates through the existing process-wide DragTracker; every other visible desktop Folder View draws the part that falls on its screen and selects the icons under it (Ctrl toggles, as on the starting screen), and clears it again when the band leaves or the drag ends.

commits.message:
containments/desktop: Continue rubber band selection across screens

Each screen's desktop has its own Folder View, so a rubber band started
on one screen stopped at its edge and couldn't select icons on the next
one. The band is now shared, so the other screens draw and select too.

BUG: 455164

media.caption: Dragging from the left screen into the right one: the band stops at the screen edge and file6-8 can't be selected
After releasing, only the left screen's icons are selected
Same drag: the band continues onto the right screen and selects file6-8
After releasing, the icons on both screens stay selected
Dragging back to the left screen: the right screen's part of the band goes away
